snip.t: Role of Intestinal Disaccharidases in Carbohydrate Digestion (10 MARKS)

qs.q: A patient with a history of chronic alcoholism develops severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Laboratory tests show elevated serum lipase. This condition impairs carbohydrate digestion primarily through the lack of which enzyme?
qs.e: Pancreatic amylase is the primary enzyme responsible for breaking down complex carbohydrates into oligo- and disaccharides.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Physiology Exam - November 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Regarding carbohydrate digestion and absorption, which of the following is correct?
o: Salivary amylase is active in the stomach.
Glucose is primarily absorbed by passive diffusion across the brush border.
SGLT1 is a transporter responsible for glucose and galactose absorption.
qs.e: SGLT1 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 1) is a secondary active transporter on the apical membrane of enterocytes that absorbs glucose and galactose along with sodium. Fructose uses GLUT5 for facilitated diffusion. Salivary amylase is inactivated by gastric acid.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - March 27, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: The final products of carbohydrate digestion absorbed by the small intestine are primarily:
qs.e: Carbohydrates are digested by amylase and brush border disaccharidases into their simplest forms, monosaccharides (glucose, galactose, fructose), which are then absorbed into the enterocytes.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - March 27, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Which statement about carbohydrate digestion and absorption is correct?
o: All dietary carbohydrates are absorbed exclusively as monosaccharides.
Fructose absorption requires the presence of insulin.
Lactase is a pancreatic enzyme that breaks down lactose.
Glucose and galactose are absorbed into enterocytes via SGLT1.
qs.e: Lactase is a brush border enzyme, not pancreatic, that breaks down lactose. Glucose and galactose are absorbed into enterocytes via the SGLT1 co-transporter (Na+-glucose cotransporter). Fructose is absorbed via GLUT5 by facilitated diffusion, independently of insulin. While most digestible carbohydrates are ultimately absorbed as monosaccharides, some dietary carbohydrates (e.g., fiber) are not absorbed at all.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - March 20, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
